cards.definition: The integration of digital technology into all areas of a business or society, fundamentally changing how it operates.
A system or device designed to be easy to use, even for people with little technical knowledge.
cards.translation: Giao diện thân thiện với người dùng

cards.definition: The newest and most advanced technology available in a particular field.
The aspect of information technology that relates to the right of individuals to control how their personal information is collected and used.
Computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as visual perception and decision-making.
The smooth incorporation of new technology or systems with existing ones without disruption.

tip.title: Pro-Tip

sections.title: 3. Technology Grammar: Future Forms
sections.description: Using future tenses effectively to discuss technological predictions and plans.

points.title: Will for Predictions
points.function: To make predictions about future technological developments
examples: Artificial intelligence will revolutionize healthcare within the next decade.
Smart homes will become standard in most households by 2030.

points.title: Be Going To for Plans
points.function: To talk about planned technological developments or personal intentions
examples: Our company is going to launch a new app next month.
I'm going to upgrade my computer next week.

points.title: Future Continuous for Ongoing Actions
points.function: To describe actions that will be in progress at a specific time in the future
examples: This time next year, I'll be using virtual reality for remote meetings.
By 2025, most people will be working with AI assistants.

rows: The government is going to invest in digital infrastructure.
We'll be using voice recognition software in most devices.

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Future Nuance
tip.text: Use "will" for general predictions about technology trends, and "be going to" for specific planned developments.

sections.title: Technology Vocabulary Practice
sections.description: Choose the best word or phrase to complete each technology sentence.

questions.prompt: "________ involves integrating digital technology into all areas of a business, fundamentally changing how it operates."
questions.explanation: Digital transformation is organisation-wide change enabled by digital technology, not a single upgrade or installation.

questions.prompt: "A ________ is designed to be easy to use, even for people with little technical knowledge."
questions.explanation: A user-friendly interface is designed for ease of use; a complex system or difficult program contradicts that requirement.

questions.prompt: "________ refers to the newest and most advanced technology available in a particular field."
questions.explanation: Cutting-edge technology means the newest and most advanced available; old equipment and basic tools express the opposite.

questions.prompt: "________ relates to the right of individuals to control how their personal information is collected and used."
questions.explanation: Data privacy concerns control over the collection and use of personal information; public information and open access concern availability.

questions.prompt: "________ involves computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence."
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence performs tasks associated with human intelligence; manual labour and human resources are not computer systems.

questions.prompt: "________ describes the smooth incorporation of new technology with existing systems without disruption."
questions.explanation: Seamless integration means systems work together without noticeable disruption; rough connection and difficult merger imply friction.

questions.prompt: "________ technology will likely become more prevalent in healthcare diagnostics."
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence performs tasks associated with human intelligence; manual labour and human resources are not computer systems.

questions.prompt: "Companies must ensure ________ to maintain customer trust in the digital age."
questions.explanation: Data privacy protects personal information and therefore supports customer trust; exposure and open access would weaken that protection.

questions.prompt: "The new smartphone features a ________ that makes it accessible to users of all ages."
questions.explanation: A user-friendly interface is designed for ease of use; a complex system or difficult program contradicts that requirement.

questions.prompt: "________ has enabled businesses to operate more efficiently and reach global markets."
questions.explanation: Digital transformation is organisation-wide change enabled by digital technology, not a single upgrade or installation.

sections.title: Listening: Should AI Make Workplace Decisions?
sections.description: Compare competing claims about efficiency, accountability and human oversight.

audio.transcript: Automated systems can help organisations process more information than an individual manager ever could. In recruitment, for example, a well-designed tool can apply the same initial criteria to thousands of applications and identify patterns that humans might overlook. That consistency is valuable. Consistency is not the same as fairness. A system can apply a biased rule perfectly consistently, especially if it learns from historical decisions that already disadvantaged certain groups. Efficiency should not prevent applicants from understanding or challenging an outcome. I agree that transparency matters, but removing automation would return us to slower and often equally biased human judgement. The better approach is to test systems continuously and assign responsibility clearly. Yet responsibility is precisely where organisations become vague. A manager may say the algorithm recommended a decision, while the vendor says the employer chose how to use the tool. Human oversight becomes symbolic if the reviewer lacks time, authority or technical understanding. Then perhaps the real question is not whether artificial intelligence should make decisions, but which decisions can be delegated, what evidence must be recorded and who has the power to reverse an error. On that point we agree. Automation may support judgement, but accountability must remain with identifiable people and institutions.

gistQuestions.prompt: What conclusion do the speakers share?
options: AI should never be used at work
AI may support decisions, but people must remain accountable
gistQuestions.explanation: Both accept support from automation while insisting on identifiable accountability.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why can a consistent system still be unfair?
options: It may learn from biased historical decisions
detailQuestions.explanation: Consistency can reproduce a biased rule or biased historical data.

detailQuestions.prompt: When does human oversight become symbolic?
options: When reviewers lack time, authority or understanding
detailQuestions.explanation: Oversight has little value if the reviewer cannot meaningfully intervene.

sections.title: Writing Part 4: Technology Opinion
sections.description: Write a short formal response using the vocabulary from this lesson.

prompt.situation: Some people believe that technology improves our lives, while others think it creates more problems than it solves. What is your opinion? Write a short essay (80-140 words) expressing your view. Use appropriate future forms and at least 5 vocabulary words from this lesson.
prompt.referenceAnswer: In my opinion, technology will continue to bring more benefits than problems to our lives. Digital transformation has already revolutionized how we work, communicate, and access information. Cutting-edge technology such as artificial intelligence will solve complex problems in healthcare and education. However, we must ensure seamless integration of new systems while protecting data privacy. In the future, I believe we'll see even more user-friendly interfaces that make technology accessible to everyone. Although there are challenges, the potential for positive change is enormous if we approach technological development responsibly.

tip.title: B2 Writing Tip
tip.text: Use a variety of future forms (will for predictions, be going to for plans) to show sophisticated grammar control. Include linking words like "however" and "although" to present balanced arguments.
